text: Joab sent to Tekoa and brought from there a wise woman, and said to her, Pretend to be a mourner and put on mourning garments.
Now the whole clan has risen against your servant, and they say, Hand over the one who struck his brother, that we may put him to death... thus they would quench my coal that is left.
We must all die and are like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; but God devises means so that the banished is not cast out from him.
The king said, Let him dwell apart in his own house; he shall not come into my presence. So Absalom lived apart in his own house and did not come into the king's presence.
Absalom said to his servants, See, Joab's field is next to mine, and he has barley there; go and set it on fire.
Then the king summoned Absalom, and he came and bowed himself before the king, and the king kissed Absalom.
